newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Kashmiris stage protest on eve of Islamic summit.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiris stage protest on eve of Islamic summit.

text.p: About 100 Kashmiri separatists staged a protest on Saturday on the airport road used by Islamic leaders arriving for a summit in Islamabad.
Witnesses said the demonstrators, watched by two policemen armed with batons, carried large banners reading "Kashmir for the Kashmiris" to back their demand for an independent state.
The Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF), which organised the protest, urged the Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC) to support what it called the Kashmiri struggle for freedom.
The JKLF wants a separate state in the disputed Himalayan region, of which India now controls two thirds and Pakistan the rest, and says Kashmiris must decide their own future.
India says Kashmir is an integral part of the Indian union, while Pakistan wants mainly Moslem Kashmiris to be allowed to vote whether to join Islamic Pakistan or Hindu-majority India.
The top officials of the Indian and Pakistan foreign ministries are due to meet in New Delhi from March 28 to 31 to renew a dialogue that stalled over the Kashmir issue in 1994.
The OIC is holding an extraordinary summit on Sunday as part of Pakistan's golden jubilee, marking 50 years of independence since it emerged from the partition of British India in 1947.
